body:
I see the reason for limiting to certain types. I think I have a more elegant idea:
```suggestion
#define GLOBAL_GET_STATIC_CACHE(m_type, m_setting_name) ([](const StringName &p_name) -> const m_type & { \
	static_assert(is_trivially_constructible_v(m_type));                                     \
	static m_type local_var;                                                                 \
	static uint32_t local_version = 0;                                                       \
	uint32_t new_version = ProjectSettings::get_singleton()->get_version();                  \
	if (local_version != new_version) {                                                      \
		local_version = new_version;                                                         \
		local_var = ProjectSettings::get_singleton()->get(p_name);                           \
	}					                                                                     \
	return local_var;                                                                        \
})(m_setting_name)
```

```c++
// Used like
GLOBAL_GET_STATIC_CACHE(bool, "test")
```

This way, it supports all basic types (e.g. the ones you listed should all work), but still prevents misuse with `String` and the likes.

body:
I think we can make do without a lock:

```suggestion
#define GLOBAL_GET_CACHED(m_type, m_setting_name) ([](const char *p_name) -> const m_type & {\
static_assert(std::is_trivially_destructible<m_type>::value, "GLOBAL_GET_CACHED must use a trivial type that allows static lifetime.");\
static std::atomic<Pair<uint32_t, m_type>> cache;\
uint32_t new_version = ProjectSettings::get_singleton()->get_version();\
Pair<uint32_t, m_type> current_pair = cache.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
if (pair.first == new_version) {\
	return pair.second;\
}\
m_type new_var = ProjectSettings::get_singleton()->get(p_name);\
cache.store(Pair(new_version, new_var), std::memory_order_release);\
return new_var;\
})(m_setting_name)
```

From a quick test this is 3x faster than `std::mutex`, at least as long as there's few updates to the value.
This can be removed now
